chapter_title: Chương 215: Thái độ cứng rắn của Trần Quý Lương

segments.title: Chương 215: Thái độ cứng rắn của Trần Quý Lương
segments.content:
Chapter 218: 0215 Chen Guiliang's Forceful Stance. Director Shang Jing moved quickly. In just two days, he brought in more than half the cast and crew of *My Own Swordsman*.

Because his new series had already been greenlit, the crew and cast were mostly the same people.

After Shang Jing called them, everyone started registering accounts one after another. Firstly, it was to give the director face; secondly, they also found it interesting.

It was at this moment that "Kaixin001 (Hainei)" quietly became "Hainei (Kaixin001)". But the URL domain name remained unchanged to prevent users from being unable to find it on a different computer.

Yao Dazui was particularly enthusiastic. After registering her account, she even posted on her microblog for two consecutive days.

Well… let's not comment on this person.

Three months prior, the viewership ratings for *My Own Swordsman* had already broken CCTV-8's record. It was now a hit on several local satellite TV stations, and there were also numerous pirated versions online. Its popularity was terrifyingly high!

With the entire cast and crew joining "Hainei (Kaixin001)", a paid online crowd spread the news on forums and Tieba, quickly attracting a large number of new users to register.

These new users might have known about Kaixin001 before but had stuck to their familiar online communities. This time, they came to register purely for the cast of *My Own Swordsman*.

Sha Yi was especially smug. Because he had joined the earliest, he used the newly launched follow function to add a bunch of his crewmate friends: "Haha, I already have over 30,000 followers. You all need to work harder."

The replies below were all eye-rolling emojis.

Watching the immense influence of *My Own Swordsman*, Chen Guiliang suddenly thought of *Soldiers Sortie*.

He made over a dozen calls and finally, through various channels, found out about *Soldiers Sortie*: filming had started last month in Caiyun Province.

After some thought, Chen Guiliang called Wang Wei, "Old Wang, has the venture capital funding arrived?"

"It's all here," Wang Wei replied.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What are your plans next?"

Wang Wei treated this as an inquiry from a shareholder and explained in detail:

"First, increase investment in technology. Optimize the smoothness and quality of video playback. Improve the on-site video search and recommendation functions."

"Second, launch a virtual points and leveling system. Introduce rating, collection, and sharing functions. Encourage user interaction around videos to enhance user engagement and sense of belonging."

"Third, discover and support creators. For example, parody video creators like Hu Ge."

"Fourth, organize various events. For instance, themed short film competitions. I also plan to imitate *Super Girl* and hold an online video talent show."

Chen Guiliang didn't comment on these strategies, only asking, "What's your long-term strategy for those pirated series, movies, MVs, and animations uploaded by users?"

Wang Wei replied, "The view counts for popular TV series, movies, and variety shows are very high. I definitely won't delete them proactively. Even if not for the view counts, constantly monitoring and deleting them would incur labor costs. But if a copyright holder files a complaint, I'll delete them immediately."

Chen Guiliang said, "Due to the rampant copyright chaos, the state is already cracking down on online music. Even Baidu MP3, to avoid legal risks, is now cooperating with over a dozen record companies. When do you think the state will start regulating video?"

Wang Wei was silent for a moment before guessing, "Probably within a year or two."

In another year and eight months, the state would issue the "Regulations on the Administration of Internet Audio-Visual Program Services." It would contain a definitive statement on online video copyrights.

But when it was first issued, none of the major video websites took it seriously. It wasn't until copyright holders took up legal arms and sued the major video websites for infringement that the online video copyright war was ignited.

By that time, with video websites madly throwing money at buying legitimate copyrights, the licensing fee for a single episode of a TV series would skyrocket, multiplying several, even dozens of times over!

Chen Guiliang continued to lead him on, "If, two years from now, the state strengthens its regulation of online video copyrights, what do you think will happen?"

Wang Wei said, "A mad scramble to buy copyrights."

"Why not buy them in advance now? You just received a large sum of venture capital funding anyway," Chen Guiliang said. "I think you can temporarily shelve that online talent show."

Wang Wei said, "I'll think about it."

Chen Guiliang didn't force the issue. "I'm just making a suggestion. If you make a move now, you'll be buying copyrights for a song. Once your competitors react, you might not be able to get popular film and television dramas even if you have the money. I helped you look into it. A hit series like *My Own Swordsman*, all 80 episodes, can be bought in a package deal for just 100,000 yuan."

On average, buying *My Own Swordsman* at this time would cost only 1,250 yuan per episode.

After the online copyright war erupted, a hit series like this would cost at least twenty to thirty thousand yuan per episode!

As the copyright war intensified, the price would soar to two or three hundred thousand per episode!

And in 2006, you could buy a non-hit series for one or two hundred yuan an episode.

As for old, classic series, they were sold in bundles. You could buy a huge pile for a few hundred thousand yuan. On average, it was only twenty to thirty yuan an episode.

Why was LeTV able to grow so big?

Because they had been quietly hoarding copyrights since 2005. Back then, with 100,000 yuan, you could buy dozens of old series in a package deal.

Hanging up the phone, Wang Wei stared at his computer, chain-smoking glumly.

At this time, the only video websites still focused on UCG were Tudou and 56.com.

But Wang Wei knew that more competitors would soon appear.

Because just a few days ago, YouTube in the United States had just completed its Series B financing. Its post-money valuation exceeded 100 million USD!

Anything that became popular in the US was bound to have a large number of followers and copycats in China.

Wang Wei's guess was correct.

6.cn and Ku6.com were already in the process of building their websites and would launch successively in the next month or two.

Although Tudou had a first-mover advantage, this advantage was rather fragile. It had to build a wider moat in advance.

Wang Wei didn't make an immediate decision. Instead, he had his employees compile data and at the same time asked users to fill out a survey.

A week later, Wang Wei analyzed the various data.

He came to the following conclusions:

First, over 80% of new users were drawn to UCG videos, especially parody videos. Therefore, the strategy of sticking to the UCG path could not be changed; it must be used to expand the user base.

Second, the quality of UCG videos was inconsistent, and most were even junk, which couldn't attract and retain old users in the long term.

Third, the time users spent watching pirated dramas, animated series, and variety shows was more than four times the time they spent watching UCG videos. The content that truly retained users in the long run was, contrary to all of Wang Wei's expectations, those pirated videos!

What to do with Tudou's development next was already clear as day: while encouraging user-generated content, they had to hoard more film and television copyrights.

Wang Wei took the initiative to call Chen Guiliang. "I'm planning to buy the exclusive online rights to *My Own Swordsman*, *Drawing Sword*, and *Chinese Paladin*."

"Good eye," Chen Guiliang laughed. "Let me recommend a TV series that's currently filming. It's a military drama called *Soldiers Sortie*. Even the investors aren't very optimistic about it, but I think it's definitely going to be a huge hit. If you buy it now, you can get it for one or two hundred yuan per episode."

"Alright, I'll send someone to make contact," Wang Wei said.

Chen Guiliang said, "When you buy *Soldiers Sortie*, add a clause that requires the main cast and crew to register for Hainei accounts. I don't care if they use them or not, but they must register with their real names."
